root.name: King's Indian Defense: Semi-Averbakh System
root.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 g6 3. Nc3 Bg7 4. e4 d6 5. Be2 O-O 6. Be3

overview: White develops the dark-squared bishop to e3 before the knight, aiming for Qd2, Nf3 or Nge2 and a quick d5. Black usually plays 6...e5 or 6...Nc6, with 6...Ng4 hitting the bishop and 6...c5 as options. After d5 the centre locks and the game becomes the King's Indian race: Black attacks the kingside with ...f5 and White expands on the queenside with c5.

white_ideas.idea: Support the centre with Be3 and Qd2, play d5 and expand with c5 and Nb5.
Meet 6...Ng4 with Bg5 and keep the e4 pawn solid.

black_ideas.idea: Strike with ...e5 or ...c5 to fight for the centre.
After d5 swing the knight to e8 or d7 and play ...f5 and ...g5 for the kingside attack.

typical_structures.structure: King's Indian locked centre with White pawns on c4, d5, e4 against Black pawns on d6, e5, with opposite-wing play.

character.notes: The King's Indian centre-lock leads to a race on opposite wings, with pawn storms and sacrifices.

gambit.notes: No material is given in the main line.

structure.notes: After ...e5 and d5 the central pawns lock, which is the typical outcome.

approach.notes: A normal Be3 branch of the main King's Indian; standard.

level.notes: Timing of the pawn storm and defence against c5 need understanding; the move order theory is moderate.

sublines_that_differ.name: 6...Ng4 line
sublines_that_differ.how: Black chases the bishop and weakens his own kingside, giving a sharper and more tactical game.

character.reason: King's Indian structures lead to mutual attacks on opposite wings.

structure.reason: After ...e5 and d5 the centre locks and play moves to the wings.

level.reason: Less forcing theory than the main KID lines but the plans need understanding.

plans.reason: Black storms the kingside and White holds central space.
